paragraphs.sourceText: Travel websites have been around since the 1990s, when Expedia, Travelocity, and other holiday booking sites were launched, allowing travelers to compare flight and hotel prices with the click of a mouse. With information no longer 36 by travel agents or hidden in business networks, the travel industry was revolutionized, as greater transparency helped 37 prices.

Today, the industry is going through a new revolution—this time transforming service quality. Online rating platforms — 38 in hotels, restaurants, apartments, and taxis —allow travelers to exchange reviews and experiences for all to see.

Hospitality businesses are now ranked, analyzed, and compared not by industry 39 ，but by the very people for whom the service is intended—the customer. This has 40 a new relationship between buyer and seller. Customers have always voted with their feet；they can now explain their decision to anyone who is interested. As a result, businesses are much more 41 ，often in very specific ways, which creates powerful 42 to improve service.

Although some readers might not care for gossipy reports of unfriendly bellboys(行李员）in Berlin or malfunctioning hotel hairdryers in Houston, the true power of online reviews lies not just in the individual stories, but in the websites’ 43 to aggregate a large volume of ratings.

The impact cannot be 44 Businesses that attract top ratings can enjoy rapid growth, as new customers are attracted by good reviews and 45 provide yet more positive feedback. So great is the influence of online ratings that many companies now hire digital reputation managers to ensure a favorable online identity.

paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：在本节中，您将阅读一段附有十个陈述的段落。每条陈述都包含其中一个段落中给出的信息。确定信息来源的段落。您可以多次选择一个段落。每个段落都标有一个字母。回答问题并标记相应的

paragraphs.sourceText: A better credit card is the solution to ever larger hack attacks .
paragraphs.translationZh: 更好的信用卡是应对更大规模黑客攻击的解决方案。

paragraphs.sourceText: A) A thin magnetic strip (magstripe) is all that stands between your credit-card information and the bad guys. And they’e been working hard to break in. That’s why 2014 is shaping up as a major showdown：banks, law enforcement and technology companies are all trying to stop a network of hackers who are succeeding in stealing account numbers, names, email addresses and other crucial data used in identity theft. More than 100 million accounts at Target, Neiman Marcus and Michaels stores were affected in some way during the most recent attacks, starting last November.
paragraphs.translationZh: A) 薄薄的磁条（磁条）是您的信用卡信息和坏人之间的唯一屏障。他们一直在努力闯入。这就是为什么 2014 年将成为一场重大对决：银行、执法部门和科技公司都在努力阻止黑客网络成功窃取帐号、姓名、电子邮件地址和其他用于身份盗窃的关键数据。从去年 11 月开始，Target、Neiman Marcus 和 Michaels 商店的 1 亿多个账户在最近的攻击中受到了某种程度的影响。

paragraphs.sourceText: B) Swipe (刷卡) is the operative word：cards are increasingly vulnerable to attacks when you make purchases in a store. In several recent incidents, hackers have been able to obtain massive information of credit-debit-(借记）or prepaid-card numbers using malware, i. e. malicious software, inserted secretly into the retailers’ point-of-sale system—the checkout registers. Hackers then sold the data to a second group of criminals operating in shadowy corners of the web. Not long after, the stolen data was showing up on fake cards and being used for online purchases.
paragraphs.translationZh: B) 刷卡是关键词：在商店购物时，刷卡越来越容易受到攻击。在最近发生的几起事件中，黑客利用恶意软件（即恶意软件）获取大量信用借记卡或预付卡号码信息，并将其秘密插入零售商的销售点系统（收银台）。然后，黑客将这些数据出售给在网络阴暗角落活动的第二组犯罪分子。不久之后，窃取的数据出现在假卡上并用于网上购物。

paragraphs.sourceText: C) The solution could cost as little as $2 extra for every piece of plastic issued. The fix is a security technology used heavily outside the US. While American credit cards use the 40-year-old magstripe technology to process transactions, much of the rest of the world uses smarter cards with a technology called EMV (short for Europay, MasterCard, Visa) that employs a chip embedded in the card plus a customer PIN (personal identification number) to authenticate(验证)every transaction on the spot. If a purchaser fails to punch in the correct PIN at the checkout, the transaction gets rejected. (Online purchases can be made by setting up a separate transaction code.)
paragraphs.translationZh: C) 该解决方案每发放一块塑料只需额外花费 2 美元。该修复是一种在美国以外广泛使用的安全技术。美国的信用卡使用已有 40 年历史的磁条技术来处理交易，而世界其他地区则使用更智能的卡，该卡采用名为 EMV（Europay、MasterCard、Visa 的缩写）的技术，该技术采用嵌入卡中的芯片和客户 PIN（个人识别码）来现场验证每笔交易。如果买家在结账时未能输入正确的 PIN 码，交易将被拒绝。 （可以通过设置单独的交易代码进行在线购买。）

paragraphs.sourceText: D) Why haven’t big banks adopted the more secure technology? When it comes to mailing out new credit cards, it’s all about relative costs, says David Robertson, who runs the Nilson Report, an industry newsletter. “The cost of the card, putting the sticker on it, coding the account number and expiration date, embossing(凸印）it, the small envelope—all put together, you’re in the dollar range. ” A chip- and-PIN card currently costs closer to $3, says Robertson, because of the price of chips. (Once large issuers convert together, the chip costs should drop.)
paragraphs.translationZh: D) 为什么大银行没有采用更安全的技术？行业通讯《尼尔森报告》的负责人戴维·罗伯逊 (David Robertson) 表示，在邮寄新信用卡时，一切都与相对成本有关。 “卡的成本，在上面贴上贴纸，编码帐号和有效期，压印（凸印）它，小信封 - 所有这些加在一起，你就在美元范围内。”罗伯逊说，由于芯片的价格，芯片和密码卡目前的成本接近 3 美元。（一旦大型发行商一起转换，芯片成本应该会下降。）

paragraphs.sourceText: E) Multiply $3 by the more than 5 billion magstripe credit and prepaid cards in circulation in the US. Then consider that there’s an estimated $12.4 billion in card fraud on a global basis, says Robertson. With 44% of that in the US, American credit-card fraud amounts to about $5.5 billion annually. Card issuers have so far calculated that absorbing the liability for even big hacks like the Target one is still cheaper than replacing all that plastic.
paragraphs.translationZh: E) 将美国流通的超过 50 亿张磁条信用卡和预付卡乘以 3 美元。 Robertson 表示，考虑到全球范围内的信用卡欺诈损失估计高达 124 亿美元。其中44%发生在美国，美国每年的信用卡欺诈金额约为55亿美元。到目前为止，发卡机构已经计算出，承担像 Target 这样的大规模黑客攻击的责任仍然比更换所有塑料卡便宜。

paragraphs.sourceText: F) That leaves American retailers pretty much alone the world over in relying on magstripe technology to charge purchases —and leaves consumers vulnerable. Each magstripe has three tracks of information, explains payments security expert Jeremy Gumbley, the chief technology officer of Credit Call, an electronic-payments company. The first and third are used by the bank or card issuer. Your vital account information lives on the second track, which hackers try to capture. “Malware is scanning through the memory in real time and looking for data，” he says. “It creates a text file that gets stolen. ”
paragraphs.translationZh: F) 这使得美国零售商在全世界范围内几乎是唯一依靠磁条技术来收取费用的零售商，并且使消费者变得脆弱。电子支付公司 Credit Call 的首席技术官、支付安全专家 Jeremy Gumbley 解释说，每个磁条都有三条信息。第一个和第三个由银行或发卡机构使用。您的重要帐户信息位于第二条轨道上，黑客试图捕获该信息。 “恶意软件正在实时扫描内存并寻找数据，”他说。 “它会创建一个被盗的文本文件。”

paragraphs.sourceText: G) Chip-and-PIN cards, by contrast, make fake cards or skimming impossible because the information that gets scanned is encrypted (加密). The historical reason the US has stuck with magstripe, ironically enough, is once superior technology. Our cheap, ultra-reliable wired networks made credit- card authentication over the phone frictionless. In France, card companies created EMV in part because the telephone monopoly was so maddeningly inefficient and expensive. The EMV solution allowed transactions to be verified locally and securely.
paragraphs.translationZh: G) 相比之下，芯片和 PIN 卡使假卡或盗读成为不可能，因为扫描的信息已加密（加密）。具有讽刺意味的是，美国坚持使用磁条的历史原因是曾经优越的技术。我们廉价、超可靠的有线网络使通过电话进行的信用卡身份验证变得顺畅。在法国，信用卡公司创建 EMV 的部分原因是电话垄断的效率低得令人发狂，而且成本高昂。 EMV 解决方案允许在本地安全地验证交易。

paragraphs.sourceText: H) Some big banks, like Wells Fargo, are now offering to convert your magstripe card to a chip-and-PIN model. (It’s actually a hybird (混合体）that will still have a magstripe, since most US merchants don’t have EMV terminals.) Should you take them up on it? If you travel internationally, the answer is yes.
paragraphs.translationZh: H) 一些大银行，如富国银行，现在提供将您的磁条卡转换为芯片和 PIN 模式的服务。 （它实际上是一个混合体，仍然有磁条，因为大多数美国商家没有 EMV 终端。）你应该接受它们吗？如果你出国旅行，答案是肯定的。

paragraphs.sourceText: I) Keep in mind, too, that credit cards typically have better liability protection than debit cards. If someone uses your credit card fraudulently（欺诈性的），it’s the issuer or merchant, not you, that takes the hit. Debit cards have different liability limits depending on the bank and the events surrounding any fraud. “If it’s available, the logical thing is to get a chip-and-PIN card from your bank，” says Eric Adamowsky, a co-founder of Credit Cardlnsider. com. “I would use credit cards over debit cards because of liability issues. ’’ Cash still works pretty well too.
paragraphs.translationZh: I) 还要记住，信用卡通常比借记卡具有更好的责任保护。如果有人欺诈性地使用你的信用卡，受到打击的是发卡机构或商户，而不是你。借记卡有不同的责任限额，具体取决于银行和欺诈事件。 Credit CardInsider 的联合创始人埃里克·阿达莫夫斯基 (Eric Adamowsky) 表示：“如果可以的话，合乎逻辑的做法是从银行获取一张芯片密码卡。” com. “由于责任问题，我会使用信用卡而不是借记卡。”现金也仍然很好用。

paragraphs.sourceText: J) Retailers and banks stand to benefit from the lower fraud levels of chip-and-PIN cards but have been reluctan for years to invest in the new infrastructure (基袖设施）needed for the technology，especially if consumers don＇t have access to it. It＇ s a chicken-and-egg problem：no one wants to spend the money on upgraded point-of-sale systems that can read the chip cards if shoppers aren’t carrying them—yet there’s little point in consumers’ carrying the fancy plastic if stores aren’t equipped to use them. (An earlier effort by Target to move to chip and PIN never gained progress.) According to Gumbley, there’s a “you-first mentality. The logjam (僵局）has to be broken.”
paragraphs.translationZh: J) 零售商和银行将受益于芯片密码卡较低的欺诈率，但多年来一直不愿投资该技术所需的新基础设施（基袖设施），特别是在消费者无法使用它的情况下。这是一个先有鸡还是先有蛋的问题：没有人愿意花钱购买升级的销售点系统，如果购物者没有携带芯片卡，该系统可以读取芯片卡，但消费者携带芯片卡毫无意义如果商店不具备使用它们的能力，就可以使用精美的塑料（塔吉特早期尝试使用芯片和密码从未取得进展。）根据甘布利的说法，存在一种“你第一的心态。必须打破僵局”。

paragraphs.sourceText: K) JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon recently expressed his willingness to do so, noting that banks and merchants have spent the past decade suing each other over interchange fees —the percentage of the transaction price they keep —rather than deal with the growing hacking problem. Chase offers a chip- enabled card under its own brand and several others for travel-related companies such as British Airways and Ritz-Carlton.
paragraphs.translationZh: K) 摩根大通首席执行官杰米·戴蒙 (Jamie Dimon) 最近表示愿意这样做，并指出银行和商家在过去十年中一直在就交换费（他们保留的交易价格的百分比）问题相互起诉，而不是解决日益严重的黑客问题。大通银行以自有品牌提供芯片卡，并为英国航空和丽思卡尔顿等旅游相关公司提供其他几种卡。

paragraphs.sourceText: L) The Target and Neiman hacks have also changed the cost calculation：although retailers have been reluctant to spend the $6.75 billion that Capgemini consultants estimate it will take to convert all their registers to be chip-and-PIN-compatible, the potential liability they now face is dramatically greater. Target has been hit with class actions from hacked consumers. “It’s the ultimate nightmare,” a retail executive from a well-known chain admitted to TIME.
paragraphs.translationZh: L) Target 和 Neiman 黑客攻击也改变了成本计算：尽管零售商一直不愿意花费凯捷顾问估计的 67.5 亿美元将所有收银机转换为芯片和 PIN 兼容，但他们现在面临的潜在责任要大得多。 Target 遭到黑客攻击的消费者集体诉讼。 “这是终极噩梦，”一位知名连锁店的零售高管向《时代》杂志承认。

paragraphs.sourceText: M) The card-payment companies MasterCard and Visa are pushing hard for change. The two firms have warned all parties in the transaction chain 一merchant, network, bank —that if they don’t become EMV-compliant by October 2015, the party that is least compliant will bear the fraud risk.
paragraphs.translationZh: M) 卡支付公司 MasterCard 和 Visa 正在努力推动变革。这两家公司已警告交易链中的所有各方（商家、网络、银行），如果他们在 2015 年 10 月之前未达到 EMV 合规性，那么合规性最差的一方将承担欺诈风险。

paragraphs.sourceText: N) In the meantime, app-equipped smartphones and digital wallets—all of which can use EMV technology—are beginning to make inroads（侵染）on cards and cash. PayPal, for instance, is testing an app that lets you use your mobile phone to pay on the fly at local merchants—without surrendering any card information to them. And further down the road is biometric authentication, which could be encrypted with, say, a fingerprint.
paragraphs.translationZh: N) 与此同时，配备应用程序的智能手机和数字钱包——所有这些都可以使用 EMV 技术——开始入侵卡和现金。例如，贝宝 (PayPal) 正在测试一款应用程序，让您可以使用手机在当地商家即时付款，而无需向他们透露任何卡信息。更进一步的是生物识别认证，可以使用指纹等进行加密。

paragraphs.sourceText: O) Credit and debit cards, though, are going to be with us for the foreseeable future, and so are hackers, if we stick with magstripe technology. “It seems crazy to me,” says Gumbley, who is English, “that a cutting-edge-technology country is depending on a 40-year-old technology.That’s why it may be up to consumers to move the needle on chip and PIN. Says Robertson:” When you get the consumer into a position of worry and inconvenience, that’s where the rubber hits the road. ’’
paragraphs.translationZh: O）不过，在可预见的未来，信用卡和借记卡将与我们同在，如果我们坚持使用磁条技术，黑客也会如此。英国人甘布利说，“一个尖端技术国家依赖于一项已有 40 年历史的技术，这对我来说似乎很疯狂。这就是为什么可能要由消费者来改变芯片和 PIN 的情况。”罗伯逊说：“当你让消费者陷入担忧和不便的境地时，那就是橡胶上路的时候了。” ”

paragraphs.sourceText: 46. It is best to use an EMV card for international travel.
paragraphs.translationZh: 46.国际旅行最好使用EMV卡。

paragraphs.sourceText: 47. Personal information on credit and debit cards is increasingly vulnerable to hacking.
paragraphs.translationZh: 47. 信用卡和借记卡上的个人信息越来越容易受到黑客攻击。

paragraphs.sourceText: 48. The French card companies adopted EMV technology partly because of inefficient telephone service.
paragraphs.translationZh: 48. 法国卡公司采用 EMV 技术的部分原因是电话服务效率低下。

paragraphs.sourceText: 49. While many countries use the smarter EMV cards, the US still clings to its old magstripe technology.

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 56 to 60 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 56 至 60 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: The report from the Bureau of Labor Statistics was just as gloomy as anticipated. Unemployment in January jumped to a 16-year high of 7. 6 percent, as 598 000 jobs were slashed from US payrolls in the worst single-month decline since December, 1974. With 1. 8 million jobs lost in the last three months, there is urgent desire to boost the economy as quickly as possible. But Washington would do well to take a deep breath before reacting to the grim numbers.
paragraphs.translationZh: 美国劳工统计局的报告正如预期的一样悲观。 1 月份失业率跃升至 7. 6% 的 16 年来新高，美国就业人数减少了 598 000 个，这是自 1974 年 12 月以来最严重的单月降幅。过去三个月失去了 1. 800 万个工作岗位，人们迫切希望尽快提振经济。但在对严峻的数字做出反应之前，华盛顿最好先深吸一口气。

paragraphs.sourceText: Collectively, we rely on the unemployment figures and other statistics to frame our sense of reality. They are a vital part of an array of data that we use to assess if we’re doing well or doing badly, and that in turn shapes government policies and corporate budgets and personal spending decisions. The problem is that the statistics aren’t an objective measure of reality；they are simply a best approximation. Directionally, they capture the trends, but the idea that we know precisely how many are unemployed is a myth. That makes finding a solution all the more difficult.
paragraphs.translationZh: 总的来说，我们依靠失业数据和其他统计数据来构建我们的现实感。它们是一系列数据的重要组成部分，我们用这些数据来评估我们做得好还是不好，进而影响政府政策、企业预算和个人支出决策。问题在于统计数据并不是对现实的客观衡量；它们只是一个最佳近似值。从方向上来说，他们捕捉了趋势，但我们确切知道有多少人失业的想法是一个神话。这使得寻找解决方案变得更加困难。

paragraphs.sourceText: First, there is the way the data is assembled. The official unemployment rate is the product of a telephone survey of about 60 000 homes. There is another survey, sometimes referred to as the “payroll survey” that assesses 400 000 businesses based on their reported payrolls. Both surveys have problems. The payroll survey can easily double-count someone: if you are one person with two jobs, you show up as two workers. The payroll survey also doesn’t capture the number of self-employed, and so says little about how many people are generating an independent income.
paragraphs.translationZh: 首先，是数据的组装方式。官方失业率是对约 60,000 个家庭进行电话调查的结果。还有另一项调查，有时称为“工资调查”，根据 40 万家企业报告的工资单对其进行评估。两项调查都存在问题。工资调查很容易重复计算某人：如果你是一个人从事两份工作，那么你就会显示为两名工人。工资调查也没有统计自营职业者的数量，因此几乎没有说明有多少人正在产生独立收入。

paragraphs.sourceText: The household survey has a larger problem. When asked straightforwardly, people tend to lie or shade the truth when the subject is sex, money or employment. If you get a call and are asked if you’re employed, and you say yes,you’re employed. If you say no, however, it may surprise you to learn that you are only unemployed if you’ve been actively looking for work in the past four weeks；otherwise, you are “marginally attached to the labor force” and not actually unemployed.
paragraphs.translationZh: 家庭调查有一个更大的问题。当被直接询问时，当话题涉及性、金钱或就业时，人们往往会撒谎或掩盖真相。如果您接到电话并询问您是否受雇，并且您说是，那么您就受雇了。然而，如果你说“不”，你可能会惊讶地发现，只有在过去四个星期内你一直在积极寻找工作，你才算失业；否则，你只是“边缘依附于劳动力”，而不是真正失业。

paragraphs.sourceText: The urge to quantify is embedded in our society. But the idea that statisticians can then capture an objective reality isn’t just impossible. It also leads to serious mis judgments. Democrats and Republicans can and will take sides on a number of issues, but a more crucial concern is that both are basing major policy decisions on guesstimates rather than looking at the vast wealth of raw data with a critical eye and an open mind. 注意：此部分试题请在答题卡2 上作答。
paragraphs.translationZh: 量化的冲动根植于我们的社会。但统计学家能够捕捉客观现实的想法并非不可能。这也会导致严重的错误判断。民主党和共和党可以而且将会在许多问题上选边站，但更重要的担忧是，双方都将重大政策决策建立在猜测的基础上，而不是以批判的眼光和开放的心态来看待大量的原始数据。

Questions 61 to 65 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 61 至 65 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: At some point in 2008, someone, probably in either Asia or Africa, made the decision to move from the countryside to the city. This nameless person pushed the human race over a historic threshold, for it was in that year that mankind became, for the first time in its history, a predominantly urban species.
paragraphs.translationZh: 2008 年的某个时候，有人（可能来自亚洲或非洲）决定从农村搬到城市。这个无名的人将人类推向了一个历史性的门槛，因为正是在那一年，人类在其历史上第一次成为一个以城市为主的物种。

paragraphs.sourceText: It is a trend that shows no sign of slowing. Demographers (人口统计学家）reckon that three-quarters of humanity could be city-dwelling by 2050, with most of the increase coming in the fast-growing towns of Asia and Africa. Migrants to cities are attracted by plentiful jobs, access to hospitals and education, and the ability to escape the boredom of a farmer’s agricultural life. Those factors are more than enough to make up for the squalor (肮脏.), disease and spectacular poverty that those same migrants must often at first endure when they become urban dwellers.
paragraphs.translationZh: 这一趋势没有放缓的迹象。人口统计学家估计，到 2050 年，四分之三的人口可能居住在城市，其中大部分增长来自亚洲和非洲快速发展的城镇。大量的工作、就医和教育的机会以及摆脱农民农业生活的无聊的能力吸引了移民到城市。这些因素足以弥补这些移民所面临的肮脏、疾病和巨大的贫困。当他们成为城市居民时，往往首先必须忍受。

paragraphs.sourceText: It is the city that inspires the latest book from Peter Smith. His main thesis is that the buzz of urban life, and the opportunities it offers for co-operation and collaboration, is what attracts people to the city, which in turn makes cities into the engines of art, commerce, science and progress. This is hardly revolutionary, but it is presented in a charming format. Mr. Smith has written a breezy guidebook, with a series of short chapters dedicated to specific aspects of urbanity—parks, say, or the various schemes that have been put forward over the years for building the perfect city. The result is a sort of high-quality, unusually rigorous coffee-table book, designed to be dipped into rather than read from beginning to end.
paragraphs.translationZh: 正是这座城市为彼得·史密斯的最新著作提供了灵感。他的主要论点是，城市生活的喧嚣及其提供的合作和协作机会是吸引人们来到城市的原因，这反过来又使城市成为艺术、商业、科学和进步的引擎。这算不上革命性的，但它以一种迷人的形式呈现。史密斯先生写了一本轻松活泼的指南，其中有一系列简短的章节专门讨论城市化的具体方面——比如公园，或者多年来为建设完美城市而提出的各种计划。结果是一本高质量、异常严格的咖啡桌书，其设计目的是为了深入阅读，而不是从头到尾阅读。

paragraphs.sourceText: In the chapter on skyscrapers, for example, Mr. Smith touches on construction methods, the revolutionary invention of the automatic lift, the practicalities of living in the sky and the likelihood that, as cities become more crowded, apartment living will become the norm. But there is also time for brief diversions onto bizarre ground, such as a discussion of the skyscraper index (which holds that a boom in skyscraper construction is a foolproof sign of an imminent recession) .
paragraphs.translationZh: 例如，在关于摩天大楼的章节中，史密斯先生谈到了建筑方法、自动电梯的革命性发明、空中生活的实用性，以及随着城市变得更加拥挤，公寓生活将成为常态的可能性。但也有时间短暂地转移到一些奇怪的话题上，比如讨论摩天大楼指数（该指数认为摩天大楼建设的繁荣是经济衰退即将来临的万无一失的迹象）。

paragraphs.sourceText: One obvious criticism is that the price of breadth is depth; many of Mr. Smith’s essays raise as many questions as they answer. Although that can indeed be frustrating, this is probably the only way to treat so grand a topic. The city is the building block of civilisation and of almost everything people do；a guidebook to the city is really, therefore, a guidebook to how a large and ever-growing chunk of humanity chooses to live. Mr. Smithes book serves as an excellent introduction to a vast subject, and will suggest plenty of further lines of inquiry. 注意：此部分试题请在答题卡2 上作答。
paragraphs.translationZh: 一个明显的批评是，广度的代价就是深度。史密斯先生的许多文章提出的问题和它们回答的问题一样多。尽管这确实令人沮丧，但这可能是处理如此宏大的话题的唯一方法。城市是文明的基石，也是人们所做的几乎所有事情的基石；因此，一本城市指南实际上是一本关于大量且不断增长的人类如何选择生活方式的指南。史密斯先生的书是对一个广阔主题的精彩介绍，并将提出大量进一步的探究线索。
